label: aligned

evidence.quote:
raise Problem("isolation-operation-unsupported",
                      f"{self.binding().adapter} does not serve pause: not offered by "
                      f"this isolation class", operation="pause", unit_id=handle.unit_id)

finding: pause, resume and fork are capability operations on the isolation interface, optional per class: the base class answers a non-serving adapter with the closed problem type isolation-operation-unsupported (501) rather than degrading, each adapter declares lifecycle_offered in its binding, and a runnable check pauses a unit, resumes it and asserts the state digest recomputed before any further syscall equals the pause-time digest, with a deliberate-breakage mode that makes it fail; the boundary classes offered are a hardware-virtualised microVM unit and a no-kernel capability-granted unit, so no shared kernel is the security boundary and no one implementation's snapshot API reaches the core. Short of leading because the run records no timing, the fork success path is exercised nowhere (only the typed refusal is), the only adapter offering the operations is the simulated one while the microVM adapter declares none, and the check is not wired into the harness gate.
